medications.purpose: Renal protection and blood pressure control in CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment – ACE inhibitor for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Slows CKD progression and reduces cardiovascular events; can be used without diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment – SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with eGFR 20‑45 mL/min/1.73 m² or ACR ≥22.6 mg/mmol (TA775)

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (CKD is a CV‑risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first_line_treatment – Statin for all CKD patients

medications.dose: Reduce basal (isophane) dose by ~25% and bolus (regular) dose by ~20%; individualise thereafter
medications.nice_justification: Guideline recommends adjusting diabetes therapy when SGLT2 inhibitor is added to avoid hypoglycaemia
Hypertension management in CKD – target <140/90 mmHg (NG203 non‑pharmacological section)
Hypertension management in CKD – part of multi‑drug regimen to achieve BP target

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for potassium imbalance (ACE‑I may raise K⁺, thiazide may lower K⁺) and additive renal effects
interactions_checked.action: Check serum potassium and creatinine 1‑2 weeks after starting ramipril; adjust thiazide dose if needed

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood pressure lowering → risk of symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after 1‑2 weeks; reduce amlodipine if systolic <110 mmHg or patient feels dizzy

interactions_checked.interaction: Increased risk of hypoglycaemia due to additive glucose‑lowering effect
interactions_checked.action: Reduce insulin dose as outlined above and advise frequent glucose monitoring

interactions_checked.interaction: Amlodipine can increase atorvastatin plasma concentrations modestly, raising myopathy risk
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin 20 mg (not >40 mg) and monitor for muscle pain; check CK if symptomatic

interactions_checked.interaction: Duplicate statin therapy → excess exposure, risk of hepatotoxicity and myopathy
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue both simvastatin tablets; continue only atorvastatin

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention; patient has stage 4 CKD
Risk of lactic acidosis in severe CKD; eGFR not known but patient is stage 4
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; guideline contraindicates dual RAAS blockade
contraindications.alternative: Use either ACE‑I or ARB, not both

Serum potassium and electrolytes not available – baseline K⁺, Na⁺, bicarbonate required before starting ramipril and any future MRA

Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I, statin, or SGLT2‑i allergies before prescribing

treatment_summary: Start ramipril 1.25 mg daily (titrate) and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for renal protection, switch to atorvastatin 20 mg daily for cardiovascular risk, adjust insulin dose to avoid hypoglycaemia, continue existing antihypertensives with monitoring, discontinue duplicate simvastatin, and arrange labs (eGFR, ACR, K⁺, LFTs) and BP checks within 2 weeks.
